cases.name: gps-only-no-control
cases.desc: A GPS-only board with no control channel. Every CAN capacity figure is zero and the largest CAN payload follows from the capability bits (SPEC.md 4.2) rather than from a field -- and a client MUST NOT infer a default.

cases.name: future-minor-unknown-capability
cases.desc: Minor 7 with a capability bit this client has never heard of. A client MUST ignore the unknown bit and use everything it does understand, and a VTP/1.0 encoder MUST NOT reproduce it (SPEC.md 2).
cases.note: This vector used to declare CAN with no Control bit, which SPEC.md 4.1 now forbids and which conformance/run.py had been quietly assuming the opposite of. `can_fd` requires `can` and `can` requires `control`, so the whole chain is present here.

cases.name: rate-below-maximum
cases.desc: A device running below its ceiling: 10 Hz of a possible 25, 100 Hz of a possible 833. Current rate and maximum rate are separate fields and a client MUST NOT read one for the other.
cases.note: The only vector where the current and maximum rates differ. Without it a decoder can read gps_rate_hz from gps_max_rate_hz's offset and pass the whole corpus -- found by tools/mutate.py, not by review.

cases.name: can-without-control
cases.desc: SPEC.md 4.1 -- `can` requires `control`. A CAN device with no Control characteristic forwards nothing, because CAN_SUBSCRIBE is the only way to ask it to, so this advertises a role no client can use.

cases.name: monitor-without-control
cases.desc: SPEC.md 4.1 -- `monitor` requires `control`. MONITOR_LIST is the only way a device can say which channels it wants.

cases.name: can-fd-without-can
cases.desc: SPEC.md 4.1 -- `can_fd` qualifies how CAN frames are carried, and qualifies nothing on a device with no CAN.

cases.name: capacity-without-capability
cases.desc: SPEC.md 4.1 -- every CAN capacity MUST be zero while the `can` bit is clear. A client sizing a buffer from can_max_frames_per_s here has been told something false about a role the device does not have.

cases.name: reserved-byte-nonzero
cases.desc: Byte 20 carries a value assigned by a future minor. It held can_max_payload until SPEC.md 4.2 derived the CAN payload ceiling from the capability bits instead, so it is reserved now -- and both halves of SPEC.md 2 apply: a decoder MUST ignore it, and an encoder MUST normalise it to zero.

cases.name: short-payload
cases.desc: 23 bytes. Info is fixed-size; a truncated read MUST be rejected.

cases.name: long-payload
cases.desc: 25 bytes. Info has no extension mechanism, so trailing bytes MUST be rejected rather than ignored.
